NLTK incomplete fix: additional JVM/JAR sandbox bypass through unvalidated launcher tokens in java() command arguments

The patched options channel correctly rejects Java argument-file references such as @/path/to/args and launcher modes such as -jar . However, an additional argument channel remains: the caller-provided cmd sequence is appended to the Java command after the validated option and classpath channels, without enforcing that its first item is a Java main-class name.

I am reporting this as an additional post-fix bypass / incomplete-fix path affecting the 3.10.3 remediation, rather than as an unrelated vulnerability family.

items.title: CVE-2026-77312 — Flyto2 Core: Arbitrary file write via unguarded data.*/file.* modules (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-67429)
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-77312 affectant flyto-core (pip) (score CVSS 10).

Flyto2 Core: Arbitrary file write via unguarded data.*/file.* modules (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-67429)

The remediation for GHSA-2956 confined writes by adding a per-module validate_path_with_env_config() call to an explicit list of modules, rather than enforcing confinement centrally. Any file-writing module absent from that list — the entire data.* and file.* families here — remains an arbitrary-write primitive.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-77312 affectant flyto-core (pip) (score CVSS 10).

Flyto2 Core: Arbitrary file write via unguarded data.*/file.* modules (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-67429)

The remediation for GHSA-2956 confined writes by adding a per-module validate_path_with_env_config() call to an explicit list of modules, rather than enforcing confinement centrally. Any file-writing module absent from that list — the entire data.* and file.* families here — remains an arbitrary-write primitive. data.csv.write 's '..' -substring check is a denylist that misses absolute paths.

Arbitrary file write with attacker-controlled content and path, escaping FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR . Overwriting a Python module under the install dir, a .flyto recipe, a shell rc, a crontab, or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys yields code execution / full host compromise — the same impact GHSA-2956 was rated Critical for.

FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR is set to the intended confinement; the module writes outside it while the GHSA-2956 guard rejects the same path.

[guard] GHSA-2956 guard validate_path_with_env_config() REJECTS out-of-sandbox path [data.csv.write] wrote=True inside_sandbox=False [data.json_to_csv] wrote=True inside_sandbox=False BUG CONFIRMED (arbitrary write outside sandbox) sample content: pwn / SENTINEL_CSV Adversarial re-read (what I tried to refute it with) Central path guard? No — runtime/languages.py PathTraversalError only guards plugin entry-point loading; the GHSA-2956 fix is per-module (confirmed at image/download.py:21 ). A module without the call is unconfined. '..' check in csv_write ? Denylist; absolute paths contain no .. → bypassed (PoC uses /tmp/... ). json_to_csv / file.copy / file.move have no check at all. required_permissions=['filesystem.write'] ? A capability flag, not a path confine

Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-77369 affectant github.com/daptin/daptin (go) (score CVSS 9.6).

Daptin: Broken Access Control (IDOR) in the generic YJS collaboration endpoint

InitializeYjsResources ( server/endpoint_yjs.go ) registers two routes.

The purpose-built, correctly-secured route, registered once per file.* -typed column on every table:

A second, generic route is registered right above it, with none of those checks:

The YJS document store's content provider parses documentName using exactly the typename.referenceId.columnName convention the secure route builds internally as roomName , and uses it to fetch the real row from the database with no authorization check of its own:

Built and ran current HEAD in a clean container; created two accounts ( admin@admin.com , first signup -> admin; bob@bob.com , second signup -> ordinary, non-admin user with default permissions only):

Fixed on the default branch in daptin/daptin@ a1a3c48f . Canonical database-backed YJS rooms now use the same row lookup and existing PermissionInstance.CanUpdate/CanRead authorization for both /yjs/:documentName and /live/... routes. Update permission grants read-write access; read-only permission grants a read-only YJS session; unauthorized and missing resources fail closed with 404. Standalone non-canonical room names retain their existing authenticated, shared-by-name behavior. The initial-content provider now validates the exact canonical form, UUID, table, and file.* column before database access.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

POLITICO had reported CERT-EU had identified the attackers’ use of ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI last week warned was being used both by criminals and state-sponsored groups.

The European Commission confirmed Thursday that it had been hit by a cyberattack last month involving a publicly available artificial intelligence tool, following media reports of the incident.

Speaking to journalists, Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said the first signs of the attack were detected October 22. He described the incident as an “AI-generated cyber campaign” but did not identify the tool used or the attackers’ apparent motivation.

POLITICO first reported that the Commission had been impacted by the cyberattack. It said CERT-EU had identified the attackers’ use of ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform that the FBI last week warned was being used both by criminals and state-sponsored groups.

The attack reportedly disrupted the European Commission’s personnel systems for more than 10 days, including payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements and translation services.

A commission spokesperson confirmed to Recorded Future News they had “taken the necessary steps in response to a detected cyber campaign,” including taking several services offline as “a protective measure.”

They said they had notified affected individuals and were “preventively checking other systems” while keeping in touch with CERT-EU and the European Data Protection Supervisor.

Des individus se faisant passer pour des représentants de l’entreprise, puis pour des policiers, sont parvenus à convaincre plusieurs clients de leur remettre leur or. Selon les informations révélées par RTL et France Télévisions, le préjudice atteint au moins 765 000 euros pour six victimes identifiées . Des plaintes ont été déposées dans une douzaine de départements et de nouvelles escroqueries ont été signalées en novembre 2026.

Fondée en 1933, Godot & Fils est une enseigne française spécialisée dans le négoce de métaux précieux, la numismatique et le change de devises. Présente à travers plus de 120 agences en France, elle commercialise notamment des lingots, des lingotins, des pièces d’or et d’argent. Son activité en ligne repose notamment sur le site Achat-or-et-argent.fr, qui propose également des solutions de conservation de métaux précieux.

L’affaire remonte au mois de juin 2026. Godot & Fils informe alors des clients qu’un accès non autorisé a été détecté sur une partie de son système d’information. Les informations concernées comprennent notamment les noms, les coordonnées et les historiques de transactions.

items.detail:
Signal de veille — The Record.

Seven of 26 founding members of the caucus are Republicans, a notable number given the White House’s steadfast opposition to regulating AI.

A bipartisan group of than two dozen House lawmakers announced Thursday they are joining a new AI Safety and Innovation Caucus to confront the security risks posed by evolving and increasingly sophisticated artificial intelligence models.

The July breach of Hugging Face by an OpenAI agent that escaped a sandbox — and the subsequent Anthropic warning that its own AI models also broke out of testing environments to obtain unauthorized access to third-party organizations — have “underscored the need for Congress to better understand these risks and develop policy solutions,” according to a press release from Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA), a caucus co-chair.

“As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems, and threats to national security.”

Whitesides and co-chairs Reps. Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) and Don Beyer (D-VA) called for bipartisan collaboration to forge basic guardrails in the face of accelerating risks, citing Americans’ well-documented concerns about the technology.

Seven of 26 founding members of the caucus are Republicans, a notable number given the White House’s steadfast opposition to regulating AI. The caucus is focused on finding “targeted” solutions that will not imperil innovation, Whitesides said in a statement.

The lawmakers will push bipartisan legislation to augment AI safety and quickly respond to AI security incidents by gathering AI developers, independent experts and government officials to brief lawmakers and help develop solutions, the press release said.

Signal de veille — The Record.

The departments are partnering on the Threat Disruption Center to better triage victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks and provide a direct channel to private sector organizations that work with victims.

The Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security announced Thursday the creation of a new task force aimed at disrupting the flow of victim funds to foreign criminal networks powering scams, cybercrime and sextortion schemes that target Americans.

The departments are partnering on the Threat Disruption Center to better triage victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks and provide a direct channel to private sector organizations that work with victims.

Senior FBI official Heith Janke said Threat Disruption Center members have already worked together on efforts to warn thousands of victims before they lose money to scammers, and the center will allow them to better coordinate their efforts.

“The Threat Disruption Center builds on those efforts by providing advanced tools and operational capabilities that enable faster action at greater scale, strengthening the work of every agency on the task force,” Janke said.

TRM Labs, which is providing technology support for the effort, said that the center has already moved to take down more than 1,600 scam websites, added more than 6,600 scam-linked cryptocurrency wallet addresses to a screening network and identified 101 new fraud networks for investigation.

The center is part of the federal government’s efforts to implement an executive order issued in March centered around stopping cyber scams, which continue to siphon billions of dollars each year from unwitting Americans.

"Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. The credential security specialist polled 1000 UK workers and 250 IT execs as part of a wider survey group of 3800 across the UK, US and France to create its latest report, Misplaced Trust: Inside the Workplace’s New AI Security Blind Spot .

It found that a fifth (19%) have shared a password, API key or login credential with an AI tool or agent, while nearly half (48%) have allowed AI to perform at least one activity without seeking permission first, including accessing emails, company files and customer information.

Read more on AI risks: NCSC Publishes Guidance on Securing Agentic AI Use

Dashlane unearthed a high propensity among UK workers to use shadow AI without thinking about the repercussions for their employer.

“Our latest data shows an emerging ‘AI Colleague Effect’ where employees are overextending trust to AI systems, sharing credentials and granting access to AI agents, sometimes without fully understanding what those tools can do with the permissions they've been given,” explained Dashlane CPO, Christophe Frenet.
